intro: If you've been thinking about converting that tired, cramped bathroom into a sleek, accessible wet room, you're not alone — it's one of the most popular home improvement projects we see in Borthwickhead right now. Whether you're planning ahead for later life, recovering from a mobility issue, or simply want a beautifully modern shower space, a professionally installed wet room can transform how your home feels and functions. Done properly, it's a significant investment that adds real value to your property and makes daily life more comfortable. Done poorly, it's a waterproofing nightmare. That's why getting the right tradesperson from the outset matters so much in a small community like Borthwickhead.
localContext: Borthwickhead sits in Midlothian and has a real mix of housing stock that directly shapes how wet room installations are approached. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that characterise much of the area often come with solid floors, limited subfloor depth, and walls that need careful assessment before any tanking or tiling begins. These homes weren't designed with wet rooms in mind, so the prep work tends to be more involved than in newer builds. Modern estate properties in and around Borthwickhead are generally more straightforward, with suspended timber floors or standard concrete bases that are easier to work with, though they still require proper waterproofing throughout. Being in a moderately hard water area also matters — limescale can affect shower heads, drainage components, and glass screens over time, so many installers in this area recommend specific fittings or water softener options to keep your wet room looking its best long-term.
serviceDetail: A full wet room installation in Borthwickhead typically begins with a detailed site survey, where the installer assesses your existing bathroom layout, floor structure, drainage options, and wall condition. This is especially important in older stone-built properties where moisture in walls or uneven floors can cause problems later if not identified early. Once a design is agreed, the work usually starts with stripping out the existing bathroom completely. If the floor is timber, a suitable deck board or screed is laid to create a level, stable base. The drainage channel or central drain point is then positioned and connected into your existing waste system — getting the fall of the floor exactly right at this stage is critical to avoid pooling water. After that, the entire floor and walls are tanked using a specialist waterproofing membrane system, applied in layers and allowed to cure fully before anything else happens. Tiling follows, covering both the floor and walls to the specified height, with all grout lines sealed properly. Finally, the shower fixtures, screen or frameless glass panel, thermostatic valve, and any heated towel rail or underfloor heating are fitted and tested. In Borthwickhead properties, the full installation typically takes four to seven working days depending on the complexity and size of the room.
pricing: Wet room installation costs in Borthwickhead generally fall between £6,500 and £12,000 for a full project, including labour, waterproofing, tiling, and fittings. Simpler modern estate homes with straightforward floor structures sit toward the lower end. Older stone-built properties or period cottages requiring extensive prep work, floor levelling, or replastering will push costs higher. The quality of your chosen tiles, shower valve, and glass screen makes a significant difference too — budget fittings versus premium brushed brass or chrome can add or save £1,000 or more. Underfloor heating, if added, typically costs an extra £400–£800. Always get a written quote that specifies materials, waterproofing system, and aftercare.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickhead and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for a project like this. They'll have worked in similar stone-built cottages and understand the quirks — thick walls, old drainage layouts, and subfloor surprises — that can catch out someone unfamiliar with the area's housing stock. Local tradespeople also have relationships with nearby suppliers, which means fewer delays and easier access to replacements if something needs changing mid-project. And if something does go wrong after completion, a local installer is far easier to get back on-site quickly than someone who travelled from the other side of the country.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwickhead?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than a modern property. Stone walls need careful assessment for moisture and may need treating or re-rendering before tanking. Solid floors are often easier to work with than old timber subfloors, but the installer needs to check the drainage fall is achievable. An experienced tradesperson familiar with Borthwickhead's older housing stock will know what to look for.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwickhead?
faqs.a: Most installations in Borthwickhead take between four and seven working days. Simpler, newer properties tend to be at the shorter end, while period cottages or stone-built homes with more complex prep work can take longer. Your installer should give you a realistic timeline after the initial survey, and you should plan for the bathroom to be out of use for the full duration.

faqs.q: Will limescale be a problem in my Borthwickhead wet room?
faqs.a: Borthwickhead is in a moderately hard water area, so limescale can build up on glass screens, shower heads, and chrome fittings over time. It's not severe, but it's worth asking your installer about scale-resistant coatings for glass and choosing quality fittings with easy-clean surfaces. Some homeowners also fit an inline filter or small water softener, which keeps the wet room looking cleaner for longer with less effort.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a property in Borthwickhead?
faqs.a: A well-installed wet room generally adds appeal and value, particularly in Borthwickhead's mix of period cottages and family homes where accessible, modern bathrooms are desirable. The key word is 'well-installed' — a poorly waterproofed wet room that develops damp issues will do the opposite. Investing in quality materials and a proper membrane system means the installation holds up over time and is an asset when you come to sell.
